evidence: privileged Telegram commands were accepted from any sender
a stranger could queue a work order or an approval for a non-owner; fixed by requiring a configured owner id and failing closed when TELEGRAM_ADMIN_IDS is unset
proposals.rationale: the webhook read the sender id into `user` and discarded it, so `/approve`, `/do` and inline Approve buttons worked for anyone who knew the chat id
proposals.title: Fix web/telegram-authz: privileged Telegram commands were accepted from any sender

evidence: open PR #27 carries a stale relay_loop.py that reverts two fixes
merging it as-is would reintroduce head-of-queue starvation and drop the feed error detail; its liveness/backoff and NEWS_TOP_STORY_ONLY changes must be re-extracted instead
proposals.rationale: the PR branched before the batch-cap starvation fix and the `_reason(exc)` feed diagnostics landed, and its merge-base predates 11 commits now on main
proposals.title: Fix scripts/relay_loop.py: open PR #27 carries a stale relay_loop.py that reverts two fixes

evidence: the documented daily heartbeat never ran
the owner heard nothing from Genesis unless they messaged it first; fixed by a daily cron
proposals.rationale: it relied on an in-run interval (RELAY_HEARTBEAT_HOURS=24) inside a relay run that lasts only RELAY_RUN_SECONDS=19800 (5h30m), so the interval could never elapse, and heartbeat.yml had no cron
proposals.title: Fix relay/heartbeat: the documented daily heartbeat never ran

evidence: /status and /help never reached the user
a user asking for status got silence; fixed by parking only the harness-owned verbs
proposals.rationale: `parse_command` matches both verbs, so they were parked on the owner-command queue and the bot's own status/help replies were unreachable dead code
proposals.title: Fix web/telegram-routing: /status and /help never reached the user

evidence: TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured
anyone who learns the Space URL can post forged Telegram updates; needs an owner-only repo secret and Space env var
proposals.rationale: the shared-secret check is present but allows every request when the variable is unset
proposals.title: Fix web/telegram-secret: TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured

evidence: agent pull requests receive no CI checks at all
verified across 6 github-actions[bot] PRs (#25, #26, #28, #30, #33, #34) with 0 check runs each, against 2 check runs on every human-authored PR; a reviewer sees no lint or test signal
proposals.rationale: the self-improvement harness opens PRs with the default GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses the events that token creates to prevent workflow loops, so `on: pull_request` never fires for them
proposals.title: Fix ci/agent-pr-checks: agent pull requests receive no CI checks at all

evidence: test_allowed_via_kernel_role fails with assert False
a red test in the V6 suite masks real regressions in the same file
proposals.rationale: a kernel-role file.read is denied where the test expects it allowed
proposals.title: Fix tests/test_tools.py: test_allowed_via_kernel_role fails with assert False

evidence: reply, command and task queues live on volatile /tmp
a queued reply, an owner command or a parked work order is lost on restart; the Space exposes no persistent volume to point them at
proposals.rationale: TELEGRAM_REPLY_QUEUE, TELEGRAM_COMMAND_QUEUE and TELEGRAM_TASK_QUEUE are hardcoded to /tmp, which a container restart discards
proposals.title: Fix web/telegram-queue: reply, command and task queues live on volatile /tmp

evidence: the review cap could be exceeded when the PR count was unreadable
the loop could open a PR past SELF_IMPROVE_MAX_OPEN_PRS; fixed by failing closed
proposals.rationale: `open_agent_prs()` returned `[]` for a non-list /pulls body, and `_github` let DNS/TLS/timeout errors escape, so a failed read looked like 'no open PRs'
proposals.title: Fix self-improve/pr-cap: the review cap could be exceeded when the PR count was unreadable

evidence: ci/test-suite
proposals.rationale: the suite carries 20 pre-existing failures from missing optional deps (redis, discord, survival); an allow-list would make a new failure visible instead of blending into the count
proposals.title: pin the baseline failures so new ones cannot hide

evidence: self-improve/verification
proposals.rationale: the dispatch fix is unit-tested, but only a live run proves a real agent PR receives its checks; a smoke check would close that gap
proposals.title: assert that an agent PR ends up with CI checks, end to end
